title: The Last Lift
scene: The St. Vale Hotel, 9:45 PM. A guest disappeared from the eleventh floor while the lobby cameras went dark.

clues.text: The hotel's only elevator was mechanically locked against all movement from 9:00 to 10:00 PM.
A guest checked into room 1104 at 8:47 PM.
The lobby camera stopped recording at 9:18 PM.
A silver suitcase was located on the eleventh-floor landing.
The elevator's authenticated motor log records a completed trip to floor eleven at 9:32 PM.
The night porter clocked in at 9:40 PM.

why: The only elevator cannot be mechanically locked against all movement for the entire hour and also complete a verified trip during that same hour.
hints: The contradiction involves motion, not the missing guest.
Compare the building maintenance report with the motor's own log.

title: Dead Air
hook: Someone heard a voice that couldn't travel.
scene: North Harbor Radio Station, 12:40 PM. A caller insists the missing host's voice was broadcast live after noon.

clues.text: The host's public interview was scheduled for 12:30 PM.
The station's only transmitter had no power or backup from noon until 1:00 PM.
The producer arrived at the studio at 11:55 AM.
A red notebook remained beside the microphone.
The control-room door was unlocked at 12:10 PM.
The transmission archive confirms a live broadcast through that transmitter at 12:22 PM.

why: The station's only transmitter cannot be unpowered with no backup and simultaneously broadcast a live signal through that same transmitter.
hints: Follow the signal path.
One statement says the only transmitter was off; another says it transmitted.

title: Five Vials
hook: The same moment. Two impossible counts.
scene: A research laboratory's specimen cabinet was photographed before anyone entered the room.

clues.text: The morning lab team left at 8:00 AM.
The cabinet was sealed and unchanged throughout the 9:15 AM inspection.
A verified image shows exactly four vials in the sealed cabinet at 9:15 AM.
A simultaneous verified image shows exactly five vials in that same sealed cabinet at 9:15 AM.
The cabinet's only label reads C-19.
A new technician received a key after the inspection.

why: Two accurate, simultaneous inventories of the same unchanged sealed cabinet cannot report both exactly four and exactly five vials.
hints: Ignore the time of day; focus on quantity.
Both counts refer to the exact same cabinet at the exact same instant.

title: Train Seven
hook: A departure after the last departure.
scene: A sleepy station, a vanished ticket, and a platform that should have gone quiet.

clues.text: The exception-free operating record says the final train of the day departed this station at 11:10 PM.
A passenger bought a one-way ticket at 10:49 PM.
Fog covered the east platform after 11:00 PM.
The same operating record verifies a train departed this station at 11:37 PM that day.
A porter collected a green umbrella in the waiting room.
Platform gate three was closed for repairs.

why: The station's published, exception-free departure log cannot identify 11:10 PM as the day's final train and also verify another departure from the station at 11:37 PM.
hints: Look at the word 'last'.
The station's own timeline contradicts itself.

title: The Vanished Bridge
hook: The chase ended somewhere that no longer existed.
scene: A river town has only one crossing. Witnesses disagree about what they saw before dawn.

clues.text: The town has one bridge and no ferry crossing.
The bridge roadway was entirely removed before 4:00 AM and not replaced until after sunrise.
A delivery van parked near the river at 3:58 AM.
There was no fog at the river.
Authenticated continuous footage shows a sedan driving across that bridge at 4:25 AM.
A call was placed from the south bank at 4:31 AM.

why: A vehicle cannot drive across the town's only bridge at 4:25 AM when that bridge's roadway had been completely removed before the hour began.
hints: A roadway is the deciding detail.
Compare the roadworks record with the authenticated crossing footage.

title: The Ninth Guest
hook: Eight seats. Nine people. No room for ambiguity.
scene: A dinner's final headcount is sealed in two independent reports.

clues.text: At 8:30 PM, each of the room's exactly eight available seats held one different guest, with no shared seats.
Dinner was served at 8:15 PM.
The only main course was mushroom risotto.
A violinist performed in the adjoining hallway.
A silver tray appears in a photograph of the room.
At precisely 8:30 PM, nine different guests were each seated in those same eight seats, with nobody standing.

why: If exactly eight seats each contain one different guest, and all nine different guests are seated only in those seats at the same instant, both reports cannot be true.
hints: This is a capacity contradiction.
Count the people, then count the seats they're each said to occupy.

title: The Dry Storm
hook: A cloudless report with a soaking-wet secret.
scene: The museum courtyard was under continuous weather surveillance.

clues.text: The courtyard's glass roof had been removed in the summer.
The verified courtyard weather log recorded zero rainfall from 3:00 to 4:00 PM.
A guard carried an umbrella at 3:20 PM.
An equally verified courtyard gauge recorded measurable rainfall there at 3:31 PM.
The courtyard had a watering hose.
The museum closed at 5:00 PM.

why: The same accurately measured courtyard cannot have zero rainfall during the entire hour and measurable rainfall occurring there at 3:31 PM within that hour.
hints: Both instruments are described as accurate.
Compare the total rainfall record with the minute-level reading.

title: Key Seven
hook: No duplicates. No exceptions. One impossible entry.
scene: A private archive's electronic access system kept a record of every accepted key.

clues.text: The archive occupies one floor.
The night custodian clocked in at 5:42 PM.
Key seven was permanently disabled at exactly 6:00 PM and could not be reactivated or bypassed.
The west hallway camera faced the loading dock.
The verified access controller accepted key seven as authorized at 6:13 PM.
A sealed folder was found beside the front desk.

why: If key seven was permanently and completely disabled at 6:00 PM with no reactivation possible, a verified successful authorization by that same key at 6:13 PM cannot occur.
hints: Trace the credential, not the visitor.
One record concerns key seven's permanent disablement; the other its later successful use.

title: The Clocktower
hook: Everyone heard the bell. Nobody touched its power.
scene: The city square's great clock has one chime system and no backup mechanism.

clues.text: The clocktower rises above the west side of the square.
The only bell mechanism was physically disconnected and incapable of sounding from 6:00 to 7:00 PM.
A parade passed the square at 6:18 PM.
The watchmaker stayed inside the workshop.
A calibrated sensor confirms the tower's bell mechanism itself struck at 6:30 PM.
Two tower windows were open until dusk.

why: The only chime mechanism cannot be physically disconnected and unable to sound from 6:00 to 7:00 PM yet produce its confirmed bell strike at 6:30 PM.
hints: Separate what people remember from what the mechanism did.
The maintenance tag and the sound sensor refer to the same mechanism.

title: The Sealed Letter
hook: A confession supposedly emerged from an envelope nobody opened.
scene: A sealed courier envelope and two equally precise chain-of-custody records.

clues.text: The only envelope opening was protected by a tamper-proof seal that stayed intact from 10:00 to 11:00 AM; contents could not pass through the intact envelope.
The courier reached the courthouse at 10:42 AM.
The receptionist wore a gray badge.
The envelope had a blue postage stamp.
The envelope rested on a wooden desk until collection.
A verified custody record says the original letter was physically removed from that same envelope at 10:30 AM.

why: A message cannot be physically removed from a tamper-proof envelope that remained sealed and intact throughout the same interval, if opening is the only way to remove it.
hints: The seal's physical properties matter.
One record says extraction was physically impossible; the other confirms it happened.

title: Frame 211
hook: Someone filmed a room in complete darkness—but the secret isn't the dark.
scene: Investigators found an apparently flawless internal recording during a building-wide outage.

clues.text: The north hallway leads to a locked archive.
The fire drill was booked for the following day.
Camera C-12's only energy supply was physically disconnected from 2:00 to 3:00 AM; it had no battery or backup.
The authenticated internal memory of camera C-12 shows a newly captured live frame at 2:26 AM.
A silver pen was found under a chair.
The camera lens was cleaned at 1:30 AM.

why: A security camera with no battery or alternative energy source cannot run during the exact period its sole mains supply was physically disconnected and record a live internal frame.
hints: Cameras can see in the dark; powering one is different.
Look for a contradiction about available electricity.

title: The Double Measure
hook: The evidence disagrees with itself to the gram.
scene: A museum weighs a sealed artifact before the auction, using one calibrated scale.

clues.text: The museum's auction opened at noon.
At 11:00:00 AM, the exact mass of the sealed unchanged artifact on the calibrated scale was 4.000 kg.
A guard signed the visitor book.
The artifact's display case was polished on Friday.
At the same instant, on that same calibrated scale under identical conditions, the exact mass of the artifact was 6.000 kg.
The auction catalog listed the artifact as item seven.

why: The same sealed, unchanged artifact cannot simultaneously have an exact mass of 4.000 kg and 6.000 kg on one calibrated scale under identical conditions.
hints: Don't be distracted by the auction.
Focus on simultaneous measurements of the same unchanged object.
